card: Updates the scanblocks RPC to throw an error when reading block filters fails instead of silently skipping blocks and returning completed: true. Previously, scans across unindexed or unreadable blocks returned partial results indistinguishable from a clean scan with zero matches. The RPC now raises an error indicating indexing is in progress if the index has not reached the range, or an internal error if the failure occurs on an already-synced range.
changed_since_previous: The implementation now explicitly calls BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain() before the scan loop, and test coverage was expanded to cover assumeutxo snapshot sync boundaries and filter file deletion.
evidence: PR description: 'The result is a silent gap: a caller gets a relevant_blocks list that looks fine but is missing any match in the unindexed range, with no way to distinguish "no matches" from "range was never scanned".'
PR description includes reproduction steps demonstrating scanblocks returning completed: true with missing matches on an unsynced node.
problem: When scanblocks queries blocks whose filters have not been indexed yet (such as during background index rebuilds or assumeutxo background validation) or cannot be read from disk, LookupFilterRange fails. The RPC previously ignored the return value, skipped the entire chunk, and still reported completed: true, silently returning incomplete match results with no indication that blocks were omitted.

risk.why: A flaw in the index sync check or error handling could reject valid scan requests or cause RPC calls to fail or hang.

summary: Throws an RPC error from scanblocks when reading a block filter range fails instead of silently skipping the unread blocks. If the filter index is still syncing or does not yet cover the range, it throws an RPC_MISC_ERROR; if the range is already covered by a synced index, it throws RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR indicating index corruption.
